children.title: Hysteresis vs. Memory in Autocatalytic Reaction Networks

detail.title: Hysteresis vs. Memory in Autocatalytic Reaction Networks
detail.summary: Recent findings refine the algebraic criteria for irreducible autocatalytic networks, clarifying that these networks can sustain bistable, history-dependent states. These states function as a form of non-equilibrium memory, which can be distinguished from simple environmental transient responses through specific stoichiometric submatrix constraints.
detail.reason: Incorporating new algebraic conditions on stoichiometric matrices to refine the distinction between simple hysteresis and functional chemical memory.
